title: At 4, Treesha Thosar Breaks Kamal Haasan's Record as Youngest National Award Winner
excerpt: Treesha Vivek Thosar received the Best Child Artist honour at the 71st National Film Awards for her role as Chimi in the Marathi film Naal 2, surpassing a record Kamal Haasan had held since 1960.
body:
• Treesha Vivek Thosar, 4, received the National Film Award for Best Child Artist at the 71st National Film Awards for her performance as Chimi (Revati) in the Marathi film Naal 2.
  • She is the youngest recipient in the history of the National Film Awards, breaking the record Kamal Haasan had held for more than six decades after winning at age six for Kalathur Kannamma (1960).
  • Treesha shot the film when she was around three. The honour includes the Swarna Kamal (Golden Lotus), a certificate, and a cash prize, and was presented by President Droupadi Murmu at Vigyan Bhavan, New Delhi, on 24 September 2025.
  • Kamal Haasan personally congratulated her on X and in a video call, telling her she had beaten his record.
  • She shared the Best Child Artist honour with Sukriti Bandireddi (Gandhi Thatha Chettu), Kabir Khandare (Gypsy), and fellow Naal 2 actors Shrinivas Pokale and Bhargav.

The youngest winner ever

On 24 September 2025, a four-year-old in a white saree walked onto the stage at Vigyan Bhavan in New Delhi and collected one of Indian cinema's highest honours. Treesha Vivek Thosar received the National Film Award for Best Child Artist from President Droupadi Murmu for her role as Chimi, also known as Revati, in the Marathi film Naal 2. The hall erupted in applause that reportedly matched the reception given to veteran stars such as Shah Rukh Khan and Rani Mukerji, honoured at the same ceremony.

The 71st National Film Awards, which recognise films certified in 2023, drew 332 feature film entries from across India. Treesha's win stood out for the naturalism of her performance — she was around three when the film was shot. After the ceremony, she told reporters she was happy the President had congratulated her, and described the evening on social media as unforgettable and joyous.

Context & background

Naal 2, directed by Sudhakar Reddy Yakkanti and produced by Nagraj Manjule, continues the story of its predecessor by exploring childhood and sibling bonds in a rural Maharashtrian village. Through the character of Chimi, the film portrays innocence, family warmth, and the emotional texture of rural childhood — qualities the jury praised in Treesha's performance.

Treesha made her acting debut with Naal 2 in 2023 and first gained wider public attention through the television serial Aai Tuljabhavani in 2024, followed by the crime series Manvat Murders. The Best Child Artist category was shared widely this year: besides Treesha, it went to Sukriti Bandireddi for Gandhi Thatha Chettu, Kabir Khandare for Gypsy, and her Naal 2 co-stars Shrinivas Pokale and Bhargav.

Impact & analysis

The record Treesha broke was one of the most enduring in Indian cinema. Kamal Haasan was six when he won the President's Gold Medal for his performance in the 1960 Tamil film Kalathur Kannamma — a record that stood for more than 60 years until a four-year-old surpassed it. Haasan did not miss the moment. Taking to X, he wrote: "Dear Ms. Treesha Thosar, my loudest applause goes to you. You've beaten my record, as I was already six when I got my first award! Way to go madam. Keep working on your incredible talent. My appreciation to your elders in the house."

"Dear Ms. Treesha Thosar, my loudest applause goes to you. You've beaten my record, as I was already six when I got my first award! Way to go madam. Keep working on your incredible talent."

— Kamal Haasan, actor, on X

The exchange went further than a post. Haasan spoke with Treesha over a video call, congratulating her, asking about her future projects, and encouraging her to stay in touch and keep working on her talent. Raaj Kamal Films International shared the conversation, describing it as a meeting between two child artistes who had both made their mark at a remarkably young age. Her performance won over the jury precisely because of its unaffected quality — the innocence of childhood, rendered without artifice.

Diaspora angle

For Indian families abroad, Treesha's win is a point of cultural pride. A four-year-old from Marathi cinema on the national stage shows diaspora children that the biggest honours in Indian film can belong to performers who look and sound like their own families — and that talent is recognised young.

"It felt great. The President congratulated me."

— Treesha Thosar, after receiving her award

What's next

Treesha is already a working actor with a growing slate. In 2025 she starred alongside Siddharth Jadhav, Mohan Agashe, and Rohini Hattangadi in the Marathi comedy crime thriller Aatli Baatmi Futli, and appeared in Mahesh Manjrekar's drama Punha Shivaji Raje Bhosale. She is set to make her Hindi debut in the heist thriller The Great Escape Faraar, opposite Nawazuddin Siddiqui.
